comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: Track a systemic fix so the playbook stays an emergency procedure**

The note documents the recovery path well, and its own root-cause sentence is the real finding:

> Root pattern: build-macos.yml build-extension derives "latest+1 at its own dispatch moment" and runs ~once daily, so any tag train landing after the daily leg has no fa-extension.zip and the gh-1832 gate correctly strands it as a draft (seen stuck: v1.0.637, v1.0.638 on 2026-10-24).

This has now bitten two consecutive releases (v1.0.637 left as a stuck draft, v1.0.638 stranded until a manual dispatch). The manual `gh workflow run build-macos.yml --ref <tag> …` + rerun dance is a fine stopgap, but as written into durable memory it risks becoming the accepted operating mode for every future tag train that lands after the daily leg. Please file a follow-up issue (and reference it here, e.g. `gh-NNNN`) for the systemic fix — cheapest options being:

- have the tag train itself produce/attach `fa-extension.zip` (or trigger the producer with the tag's version), so the gh-1832 gate never strands a draft; or
- schedule the producer more frequently than trains land / make it event-driven rather than once-daily "latest+1".

Not blocking: the note is accurate and valuable as-is.

**Key Issues**: None blocking. One suggestion: the note itself names the recurring systemic root cause (once-daily producer vs multiple-daily tag trains) — track a code/CI fix so the manual dispatch playbook stays an emergency procedure, not the operating mode.

2. Merge.
